signals.title: NASDAQ IPO Filing for $29.4B to Fund Yongin Cluster & EUV Equipment
signals.signal: SK Hynix filed with the SEC in June 2026 to raise approximately $29.4 billion through a NASDAQ listing of American Depositary Shares under ticker SKHY. Proceeds target capex for new semiconductor fabrication facilities, EUV lithography equipment (delivery target December 2027), and the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster expansion representing a 600 trillion won commitment through 2030. This marks the largest ADR offering in history, reflecting confidence in AI memory demand and capital intensity of the growth strategy.
key_points: 17.79M ADS offering (~2.5% of shares) with target price ~$166/share to raise $29.4B
Proceeds allocated to Yongin Cluster capex expansion and procurement of advanced EUV tools
SK Square retains ≥20% control via stake structure; first NASDAQ listing for SK Hynix
Yongin campus targeting 1M wafers/month DRAM capacity by 2030
signals.why_it_matters: Direct strategic signal of aggressive capacity expansion to capture AI memory supercycle. Capital raise enables accelerated build-out of Yongin and Indiana packaging, positioning SK Hynix to meet forecast 2026 HBM demand growth and lock in supply contracts. IPO raises ~$29.4B at critical moment when rival Samsung also ramping capex, sharpening competitive race.
signals.chain_link: Upstream supplier equipment (EUV lithography from ASML; construction and materials). Downstream demand (hyperscale cloud customers, NVIDIA, Google, AWS for HBM/DRAM).
stakeholders: ASML (EUV equipment supplier)
NVIDIA (largest HBM customer)
Google, AWS, Microsoft, Meta (cloud HBM demand)
SK Square (strategic parent, maintaining control)
Global institutional investors (foreign ownership ~54%)
signals.source: IBTimes AU, ibtimes.com.au/sk-hynix-nasdaq-listing; SK Hynix investor filings; NASDAQ registration statement

signals.title: Record Capex Boost: 2026 Plan KRW 35T+, Yongin 600T Expansion Multi-Decade Commitment
signals.signal: SK Hynix announced 2026 capex target of KRW 35 trillion (up from KRW 29T in 2025 and KRW 22T initial 2025 target). The Yongin Semiconductor Cluster investment expanded from original KRW 120T to KRW 600T multi-decade capital program, targeting 1 million wafers/month capacity by 2030. M15X fab in Cheongju (KRW 20T+) began equipment installation ahead of schedule in 2Q 2025. Indiana US packaging facility represents additional $3.9–5.6B investment through 2028. Capex guidance maintains mid-30% of sales ratio. This represents the largest memory chip capex cycle in SK Hynix history.
key_points: 2026 capex KRW 35T+ (up from KRW 29T 2025, KRW 22T 2025 original), maintaining mid-30% sales ratio
Yongin Cluster expanded from KRW 120T to KRW 600T multi-decade commitment with 1M wafers/month target
M15X Cheongju fab (KRW 20T+) equipment installation underway, targeting 2025 ramp completion
Indiana advanced packaging facility $3.9–5.6B capex, volume production HBM from H2 2028
signals.why_it_matters: Aggressive capex acceleration signals SK Hynix sees sustained multi-year HBM demand and commands pricing power to justify heavy investment. Capex spend of KRW 35T+ with operating cash flow ~KRW 50T constrains FCF to ~KRW 15T (30% shareholder payout rule); indicates capex prioritized over dividends. Competitive moat—if Samsung and Micron also ramp capex, supply tightness persists; if they hold back, SK Hynix gains capacity share.
signals.chain_link: Upstream: construction firms, semiconductor equipment vendors (ASML EUV, Applied Materials deposition/etch, vacuum equipment). Downstream: DRAM/HBM demand fulfillment to cloud, enterprise, AI customers.

signals.title: NVIDIA Multiyear Partnership Locked In; Co-development for Vera, RTX Spark, Jetson Thor
signals.signal: On June 7, 2026, NVIDIA and SK Hynix announced a multiyear technology partnership for next-generation memory aligned to NVIDIA's AI infrastructure roadmap. Agreement secures long-term supply of HBM for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin supercomputers, Vera CPUs, RTX Spark PCs, and Jetson Thor robotics. Partnership includes co-development of memory using NVIDIA CUDA-X and PhysicsNeMo frameworks directly integrated into SK Hynix design/manufacturing workflows. SK Hynix will also develop fab digital twins using Omniverse for autonomous fab operations. Deal announced during Jensen Huang's Seoul visit and represents deepening of existing supplier relationship into strategic co-engineering partnership.
key_points: Multiyear strategic partnership announced June 7, 2026 during Jensen Huang visit to Seoul
Codevelopment for NVIDIA Vera Rubin supercomputers, Vera CPUs, RTX Spark PCs, Jetson Thor robotics platforms
SK Hynix implementing NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries and PhysicsNeMo into memory design and fab digital twins
Extends supply relationship across AI infrastructure, personal AI, and physical AI markets
signals.why_it_matters: Locks in NVIDIA as strategic anchor customer across multiple hardware platforms beyond just HBM supply. Partnership depth—co-development of fab automation and memory architecture—raises switching costs and creates long-term revenue visibility. Signals NVIDIA confidence in SK Hynix as sole or preferred supplier for next-gen Vera ecosystem. De-risks supply risk for NVIDIA and ensures memory roadmap alignment with compute roadmap.
signals.chain_link: Downstream: NVIDIA's design and manufacturing workflow; AI factory buildout (cloud hyperscalers); personal AI edge devices.

Google, AWS, Microsoft, Meta (cloud customers buying NVIDIA)
Samsung, Micron (rival memory suppliers seeking NVIDIA traction)
TSMC (co-supplier for custom HBM base dies per SK Hynix roadmap)
signals.source: NVIDIA Newsroom (June 7, 2026); SK Hynix Newsroom; Sherwood News, TechTimes, CRN Asia

signals.title: Solidigm Acquisition (Intel NAND) Finalized; Second Phase Closed March 2025
signals.signal: SK Hynix completed the second and final phase of Intel NAND/SSD acquisition on March 27, 2025, for $1.9 billion (vs. initially expected $2B). Combined with first phase ($7B in Dec 2021), total deal value ~$8.9B. Second phase transferred Intel's proprietary NAND IP, R&D team, and technical staff for Dalian facility workforce. Solidigm (branded subsidiary) now wholly owned by SK Hynix, headquartered San Jose. Lee Seok-hee (former SK Hynix co-CEO) became Solidigm executive chairman. Enables unified NAND development across SK Hynix mobile expertise and Solidigm enterprise eSSDS leadership, targeting global 1st tier status in NAND.
key_points: Second phase closed March 27, 2025 at $1.9B (total deal ~$8.9B vs $8.84B announced)
SK Hynix acquired Intel NAND IP, R&D staff, and Dalian facility workforce; now 100% owner of Solidigm
Lee Seok-hee (former co-CEO) appointed Solidigm Executive Chairman; Rob Crooke (ex-Intel SVP) CEO
Unifies SK Hynix mobile NAND expertise + Solidigm enterprise eSSSD strength; enables dual-track NAND roadmap
signals.why_it_matters: Completes strategic acquisition to elevate SK Hynix NAND business from regional to global tier-1 status. Solidigm IP and R&D team unlocks proprietary controller and firmware tech for enterprise SSDs (eSSDs), expanding TAM beyond mobile. Enterprise eSSDS market benefiting from AI data center buildout; SK Hynix now positioned to capture share. Removes competitor Intel from NAND; consolidates market. Second phase completion enables seamless tech integration and unified roadmap execution.
signals.chain_link: Upstream: NAND wafer fabs (Dalian, SK Hynix). Downstream: enterprise SSD customers (hyperscale cloud, enterprise IT, AI storage appliance makers).

signals.title: HBM Sold Out Through 2026; 2026 Price Hike ~20% for HBM3E Amid Supply Crunch
signals.signal: SK Hynix confirmed all 2025 HBM volume sold out, with 2026 supply negotiations finalized with all major customers by late 2025. CEO Kwak Noh-jung stated HBM4 finalized 2026 volumes by June 2025. In December 2025, sources reported SK Hynix and Samsung raised HBM3E prices by ~20% for 2026 deliveries due to sustained demand from NVIDIA H200, Google TPU v7p/v7e, Amazon Trainium3, each incorporating 6–8 HBM3E stacks. HBM content per accelerator rising 20–30% vs. prior gen. Goldman Sachs estimates HBM demand for custom ASIC chips surging 82%, with HBM4 expected 55% of 2026 revenue mix vs. HBM3E 45%. Supply remains extremely tight; SK Hynix retains 50–62% market share.
key_points: All 2026 HBM supply sold out; major customer negotiations completed by late 2025 (NVIDIA, Google, AWS, Microsoft, Meta)
HBM3E prices raised ~20% for 2026 due to extended demand for H200, TPU v7p/v7e, Trainium3 ASICs
HBM content per accelerator rising 20–30%; each H200 uses 6 stacks, TPU v7 uses 8 stacks
Goldman Sachs: ASIC-based HBM demand surging 82% in 2026; HBM4 mix 55%, HBM3E mix 45% revenue
signals.why_it_matters: Price power and supply tightness directly boost revenue and operating margins. 20% price increase on sold-out 2026 volume provides significant ASP uplift; combined with volume growth (HBM shipments expected +9x vs 2023), operating profit expansion is material. However, risk: Samsung HBM4 competitive pressure. Goldman Sachs warned HBM ASP could face 5–15% headwind if Samsung/Micron capture share. Supply crunch also constrains customer ability to diversify suppliers, favoring SK Hynix short-term but creating long-term geopolitical exposure.
signals.chain_link: Downstream: NVIDIA, Google, AWS, Microsoft, Meta custom ASIC and GPU procurement; cloud data center spending decisions.

Samsung (competitive HBM4 threat; Daishin estimates 28% HBM4 share by end-2026 vs. SK Hynix 55%)
Micron (5–10% HBM share; ramping production)
signals.source: Trendforce (Dec 24, 2025); Seeking Alpha (Dec 26, 2025); DigiTimes (Dec 24, 2025); SK Hynix newsroom (April 24, 2026 market outlook)

signals.title: HBM4 Mass Production Ramp; 12-Layer Samples Shipped Q1 2025, Volume Q4 2025
signals.signal: SK Hynix completed HBM4 development in September 2024 and shipped the world's first 12-layer HBM4 samples to customers in March 2025. Mass production began Q4 2025. HBM4 features 1.5+ TB/s bandwidth per stack vs. 1.18 TB/s for HBM3E, with 48GB capacity and 3nm-based architecture. 2026 roadmap shows HBM4 16-Hi stacks and HBM4E variants. Custom HBM (cHBM) integrates GPU/ASIC functions into HBM base die, reducing data transfer power. Partnership with TSMC for custom HBM base dies. Goldman Sachs forecasts HBM4 demand for custom ASIC chips surging 82% in 2026. UBS predicts SK Hynix will capture ~70% HBM4 market share on NVIDIA Vera platform in 2026.
key_points: HBM4 development completed Sept 2024; 12-layer samples shipped March 2025; mass production Q4 2025
HBM4 specs: 1.5+ TB/s per stack, 48GB capacity, 3nm base die; custom HBM integrates controller on base
2026 roadmap: HBM4 16-Hi and HBM4E 8/12/16-Hi stacks; custom HBM with TSMC partnership
Goldman Sachs: HBM4 demand for custom ASICs surging 82%; UBS predicts SK Hynix 70% share on NVIDIA Vera
signals.why_it_matters: Maintains SK Hynix technology leadership and supply moat through next generation. Early mass production vs. competitors (Samsung in transition, Micron ramping) locks in first-mover advantage for HBM4 and custom HBM with NVIDIA, Google, AWS. Custom HBM reduces power per bit and simplifies customer design, strengthening competitive stickiness. UBS 70% market share forecast on Vera implies SKH retains dominant position through 2026+. However, downside risk if Samsung HBM4 yield improves faster or if custom HBM complexity creates ramp delays.

signals.title: CEO Leadership Transition & Solidigm Integration; Kwak Noh-Jung Sole CEO, Lee Seok-Hee to Intel
signals.signal: In June 2026, Intel hired Seok-Hee Lee, former SK Hynix co-CEO and Solidigm executive chairman, as EVP of Intel Foundry to lead advanced packaging and back-end manufacturing. Lee spent ~10 years at Intel (2000–2010) on process nodes 130nm–32nm, then led SK Hynix and acquired Intel NAND in 2020. His departure marks reorganization at SK Hynix. Kwak Noh-Jung (appointed co-CEO in 2022, sole CEO in April 2026) assumes full strategic leadership. Kwak, a 29-year Hynix veteran and semiconductor technologist (PhD Materials Engineering), leads HBM technology and 2026–2030 capex expansion. Internal stability maintained; operations and manufacturing expertise under Kwak's control; Solidigm leadership under Rob Crooke (ex-Intel SVP).
key_points: Seok-Hee Lee hired by Intel as EVP Foundry (June 18, 2026), leaving Solidigm executive chairman role
Lee's 10-year Intel history (2000–2010, 130nm–32nm), then 13-year SK Hynix/Solidigm tenure, now returns to Intel
Kwak Noh-Jung confirmed sole CEO (April 2026), 29-year Hynix technologist, PhD Materials Engineering
Solidigm leadership stable under Rob Crooke (ex-Intel SVP); SK Hynix maintains technology continuity under Kwak
signals.why_it_matters: Leadership change signals confidence in Kwak and internal bench strength; no disruption expected. Lee's departure to Intel reflects Intel's aggressive foundry turnaround (partnership with TSMC, Tesla, Google TPU packaging), but his exit at Solidigm is orderly. Kwak's sole CEO role simplifies decision-making on capex, memory roadmap, and customer partnerships. Risk: if Kwak loses key lieutenants or if Lee's networking at Intel strengthens Intel's packaging technology vs. SK Hynix's Indiana facility plans.
signals.chain_link: Anchor strategic leadership; impacts internal R&D prioritization, capex allocation, and customer negotiations.

signals.source: TechTimes (June 19, 2026); Intel press release (June 18, 2026); SK Hynix corporate governance disclosures

signals.title: AI Memory Vision Shift to 'Creator' Role; PIM, CXL Memory, Custom HBM Roadmap through 2031
signals.signal: At SK AI Summit 2025 (Nov 3–4), CEO Kwak Noh-Jung elevated SK Hynix's vision from 'full-stack AI memory provider' to 'full-stack AI memory creator.' Presented next-gen roadmap spanning three pillars: AI-D (Expansion/Optimization: HBM, LPDDR6, SOCAMM2, CXL Memory), AI-D B (Breakthrough: Processing-in-Memory PIM, CXL Memory Module, ultra-high-capacity memory to overcome 'memory wall'), and AI-N (Next-gen storage: high-performance SSDs, 321–375-layer NAND). Showcased 16-layer HBM4 48GB at CES 2026. Announced research on HBM5/HBM5E (2029–2031), DDR6, GDDR7-Next, 400+ layer 4D NAND. PIM technology reduces CPU/GPU data movement by 80% power. Partnership with TSMC for custom HBM integration. Focus on solving 'memory wall' bottleneck in AI systems.
key_points: SK AI Summit 2025: Vision elevated to 'AI memory creator' (not just provider); three-pillar roadmap through 2031
AI-D Breakthrough: PIM (reduces data movement power 80%), CXL Memory, CMM-Ax for server platforms
Custom HBM with TSMC, 16-layer HBM4 (48GB) showcased; HBM5 planned 2029–2031
Storage: 375-layer NAND in production; AI-N roadmap for high-bandwidth flash (HBF) inference acceleration
signals.why_it_matters: Broadens SK Hynix beyond commodity memory into specialized AI-optimized solutions, raising TAM and margins. PIM and CXL Memory address system bottlenecks, creating new product categories and customer lock-in. Custom HBM with TSMC partnership deepens integration with cloud and NVIDIA ecosystems. Multi-decade roadmap (through 2031) signals confidence in AI-driven memory demand. Differentiates from Samsung and Micron, who focus more on commodity HBM/DRAM. Risk: technology execution risk (PIM, CXL, custom HBM all require new fabs, IP, and customer adoption).
signals.chain_link: Upstream: TSMC (custom HBM dies), EUV and advanced lithography. Downstream: NVIDIA, cloud hyperscalers adopting PIM and custom HBM; AI inference platforms requiring high-bandwidth flash.
